findings.text: 12 chemotype(s); the largest holds 6 of 25 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 34 heavy atoms, about 162% of a typical molecule, and 24% of the set can be cut at it
the 34 shared framework atoms sit 11.3 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (6 of 25 carry them) -- the molecules are not in a common frame
the chosen attenuation 0.1 is at the bottom of the grid: the search needed a value it was not offered, so widen it before believing the model

the file has 11 numeric column(s) of its own (mw, n_papers, dG_ads, depth, mwila_hcl_adj, mwila_h2so4_raw, mwila_h2so4_adj, mwila_pooled_raw and 3 more); with them the descriptor baseline is +0.629 in q2 against the computed descriptors (95% interval +0.426 to +1.011); the activity under another name, by a correlation above 0.95: mwila_pooled_raw -- these columns predict the activity, so they are measurements or forms of the activity and not descriptions of the structure. They are not used. If some of them are real descriptors, such as the conditions of the measurement, name them (descriptors=..., or --descriptors on the command line) and run again
the aligned model is +0.202 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.400 to +1.096) -- the frame gains nothing over counts
the aligned model is -0.198 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.611 to +0.106) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.087 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -0.586 to +0.327) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry adds nothing on this set

why: descriptors alone match the 3D model, so a field model here is an expensive way to count atoms; use the fields only if the co-field is the purpose
